title: Inference Unit Chain Hard Proof
subtitle: Prove the controller-owned maximal lifecycle chain composes.
scope: Deterministic hard proof for inference-unit chaining in the standalone living-doc harness.
sourceCoverage: Created from the May 14, 2026 session that identified partial inference-unit chaining tests, report evidence, GitHub issues #300 and #301, and the existing contract-bound inference unit type-system living doc as source context.
objective: Prove that the living-doc harness can deterministically coordinate the hardest inference-unit lifecycle chain as one controller-owned composition, using mock or fake-headless unit execution with the same input contracts, output contracts, validations, and artifact layout as real units, from unresolved work through repair, worker re-entry, commit-intent, PR-review, closure-review, and controller-persisted terminal closure, with generated HTML and JSON evidence showing the actual chain timeline and gate transitions.
successCondition: The objective is met only when a deterministic maximal-chain test runs locally and in CI, the generated report shows one composed controller-owned timeline with concrete unit artifacts and gate before/after state, every acceptance criterion maps to source-system evidence, and partial proofs, hand-written report prose, architecture diagrams, or suite-level coverage summaries cannot satisfy closure.

runState.nextObjectiveAction: This hard-proof living doc is complete for contract-surface coverage. Next work moves back to the contract-bound inference unit type-system living doc: run a fresh standalone lifecycle to prove cross-run artifact references in the real harness path.

objectiveFacets.name: Maximal chain composition
objectiveFacets.description: One deterministic test must exercise the hardest lifecycle path as a single composed controller-owned run.

objectiveFacets.name: Contract shape fidelity
objectiveFacets.description: Mock or fake-headless units are valid only when they use the same input contracts, output contracts, validation artifacts, and artifact layout as real units.

objectiveFacets.name: Controller-owned routing
objectiveFacets.description: Units emit typed claims and artifacts; the lifecycle controller selects every next unit and persists terminal state.

objectiveFacets.name: Evidence carryover
objectiveFacets.description: Output and evidence from each unit must become authoritative input to the following controller-selected unit.

objectiveFacets.name: Gate block and unblock
objectiveFacets.description: Commit and PR-review gates must prove both the blocking state and the later unblocked state in the same hard chain.

objectiveFacets.name: Terminal authority
objectiveFacets.description: Reviewer closure claims cannot close the lifecycle; closure-review approval plus controller persistence is required.

objectiveFacets.name: Negative breakpoints
objectiveFacets.description: The suite must fail deterministically at the hard-chain points where composition can break.

objectiveFacets.name: Generated report evidence
objectiveFacets.description: The HTML and JSON report must be generated from test artifacts and expose the actual timeline, not hand-authored proof language.

invariants.statement: The objective cannot close from isolated transition tests, fake-headless calibration alone, architecture prose, closed tickets, or report polish.
Inference units may produce typed claims and artifacts, but the controller must own route selection, gate decisions, and terminal persistence.
A mock or fake-headless unit counts as proof only when its input, output, validation, and artifact shape match real unit execution.
A side-effect gate is not proven by showing only the blocked or only the approved state; the hard chain must show both.

sections.title: Acceptance Criteria
sections.summary: Closure criteria for proving the hard-chain objective.

data.title: Deterministic maximal-chain test
data.objectiveTerm: deterministically coordinate the hardest inference-unit lifecycle chain as one controller-owned composition
data.criterion: A deterministic maximal-chain test runs locally and in CI as one composed lifecycle path, not a set of isolated finalizer calls.
data.proofRequired: A test file and generated report entry for the maximal chain, run by `npm run test:harness-chaining-report` and covered by `npm run test:contract`.
data.acceptanceTest: The report shows one named maximal-chain timeline containing repair, worker re-entry, commit-intent, PR-review, closure-review, and terminal closed.

data.title: Controller-owned routing
data.criterion: Every transition in the maximal chain is selected by controller routing from validated contracts and evidence, not by a unit directly invoking the next unit.
data.proofRequired: Selection artifacts for each step showing current unit, selected next unit, gate reason, and validation status.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if a unit bypasses controller selection or if a selected next unit lacks a valid selection artifact.

data.title: Artifact continuity
data.objectiveTerm: same input contracts, output contracts, validations, and artifact layout as real units
data.criterion: Each unit writes prompt, input contract, result, validation, and output artifacts, and later unit inputs reference earlier artifacts as required evidence.
data.proofRequired: Generated JSON report timeline listing artifact paths for every unit and assertions that those files exist and parse.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if any required artifact is missing, malformed, or not carried into the next unit input where required.

data.title: Repair re-entry
data.objectiveTerm: from unresolved work through repair, worker re-entry
data.criterion: The maximal chain proves that repair returns to worker and the later reviewer pass observes the repaired state before closure gates proceed.
data.proofRequired: Timeline evidence showing reviewer repairable, balance scan, repair-skill result, next worker, and second reviewer consuming repaired evidence.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if the chain skips worker re-entry or if the later reviewer does not consume repair output.

data.title: Commit and PR-review gates block and unblock
data.criterion: The maximal chain proves both blocked and unblocked states for commit evidence and PR-review evidence.
data.proofRequired: Timeline evidence showing missing commit evidence selects commit-intent, later commit evidence permits progress, missing PR-review evidence selects pr-review, and later approved PR-review evidence permits closure-review.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if either gate is shown only in blocked form or only in approved form.

data.title: Terminal authority
data.criterion: Reviewer closure cannot close the lifecycle; terminal closed is written only after closure-review approval and controller persistence.
data.proofRequired: Assertions and report evidence showing reviewer closure claim, closure-review approval, and terminal state path written by the lifecycle controller.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if reviewer output alone can persist terminal closed.

data.title: Negative breakpoint matrix
data.criterion: Deterministic negative cases cover missing commit evidence, bad commit scope, missing PR review, blocked PR review, closure denial, ineffective repair, invalid next unit, and stale or mismatched evidence.
data.proofRequired: Named negative tests in the chaining suite and report, with failing condition assertions for each breakpoint.
data.acceptanceTest: The suite fails if any required hard-chain breakpoint is not represented by a deterministic negative case.

data.title: Generated report evidence
data.objectiveTerm: generated HTML and JSON evidence showing the actual chain timeline and gate transitions
data.criterion: The report is generated from test artifacts and shows test names, statuses, timings, stdout/stderr, unit sequence, artifact paths, selected next units, gate before/after state, and terminal state path.
data.proofRequired: `docs/inference-unit-chaining-test-report.html` and `.json` generated by `scripts/render-inference-unit-chaining-test-report.mjs` after running the suite.
data.acceptanceTest: The report must make it obvious that the complex chain ran as one composed lifecycle path; hand-written prose or suite-level coverage summaries do not count.

diagrams.title: Required maximal chain
diagrams.text:
flowchart LR
  W1[worker unresolved work] --> R1[reviewer repairable]
  R1 --> BS[living-doc-balance-scan]
  BS --> RS[repair-skill]
  RS --> W2[worker re-entry]
  W2 --> R2[reviewer closed claim with source changes]
  R2 --> CI[commit-intent]
  CI --> PR[pr-review]
  PR --> CR[closure-review]
  CR --> TS[controller terminal closed]
  K[harness controller] -. selects every next unit .-> R1
  K -. validates gates and evidence .-> CI
  K -. persists terminal state .-> TS
